label: neuter
reason: The definition and the parent 'sterile' (a fertility quality) are right. But the exact synonym 'asexual' does not fit: in botany 'asexual' means reproducing without sex (by spores or vegetative growth), not a flower with no working sex organs. Remove it, or at most make it a related synonym. A neuter lemma or ray flower is an empty or sterile one, so those bearers fit.

label: septifragal
reason: Matches the standard glossary meaning: the valves break away from the septa, which stay on the central column. 'dehiscent' is the right parent, alongside septicidal and loculicidal.

label: latiseptate
reason: Correct, as used in Brassicaceae: the fruit is flattened parallel to the septum, so the septum spans the widest diameter (the opposite of angustiseptate). 'flattened' is the right parent. PATO has no such term.

label: chasmogamous
reason: Correct, and the open counterpart of FLOPO:0991176 cleistogamous (which sits under 'closed'). The 'seed' bearer means a seed from a chasmogamous flower; that is a data-mapping question, not a fault in the class.

label: parasitic
reason: Correct, and it uses the same parent as FLOPO:0991334 hemiparasitic. PATO has no 'parasitic'. Because this definition says 'wholly or in part', hemiparasitic should become a child of this class; that change belongs to hemiparasitic.

label: monocarpic
reason: The definition and parent are fine and semelparous is a good synonym. 'hapaxanthic' is not an exact synonym: it describes a single stem that dies after flowering. In clustering palms such as Caryota, the stems are hapaxanthic but the plant as a whole lives on. Make it a related synonym.

label: medifixed
reason: The definition is right and matches its siblings basifixed, dorsifixed and peltate. Two synonyms do not fit. 'medifixed hair' names a part plus a quality, not a quality: remove it. 'malpighian' applies only to T-shaped hairs (trichomes attached at the middle): make it a related synonym.

label: clonal
definition: A multi-cellular organismal disposition inhering in a plant by virtue of its spreading vegetatively, by rhizomes, stolons, root suckers or bulbs, into a group of genetically identical shoots or ramets.
reason: Forming clones describes how a plant grows and reproduces (a tendency of the whole plant, like monocarpic), not its shape or build. So PATO:0000141 'structure' is the wrong parent. The meaning is right; the text is reworded to fit the new parent.

label: hypogynous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being inserted, or bearing the perianth and stamens inserted, on the receptacle below the ovary and free from it.
reason: The meaning and parent are right, but the text says 'a floral organ or flower' and then always describes the perianth and stamens. That reads wrongly when the bearer is a stamen, a perianth part or a disc. The new wording covers both the flower and its organs, in the same style as half-inferior.

label: palmatipartite
definition: A palmately lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut palmately more than halfway, but not fully, to the base into segments radiating from a common point.
reason: Wrong parent. Its pinnate counterpart FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite sits in the lobed family (under pinnatifid, which is under pinnately lobed). The matching place here is palmately lobed. Palmatifid (FLOPO:0991351) can't be the parent because it is defined as 'about halfway' only. A split depth of 'more than halfway but not to the base' also falls inside palmately divided (FLOPO:0991272).

label: barrel-shaped
reason: Correct 3-D shape (doliiform), and 'convex 3-D shape' is the right parent, the same as for PATO cylindrical-type shapes. PATO has no barrel-shaped term.

label: palmately divided
reason: Its definition ('more than halfway') overlaps palmatipartite and palmatisect, and both related synonyms are already their own classes. palmatisect is FLOPO:0991282, and palmatifid is FLOPO:0991351, which is defined as 'about halfway' and so falls outside this definition. Remove both synonyms. Either keep this as a general class with palmatipartite and palmatisect under it, or use it for 'palmatisect' as many glossaries do.

label: incumbent
definition: A positional quality inhering in a cotyledon by virtue of the cotyledon's back lying against the radicle, which is folded along it.
reason: The cotyledon meaning (notorrhizal, the counterpart of accumbent FLOPO:0991331) is correct. But the 'anther' bearer is a different meaning: an anther turned inward against the filament. That is two meanings in one class, so map anther statements elsewhere. Also: notorrhizal is listed as both an exact and a related synonym; the wording should match accumbent's.

label: pseudopeltate
reason: Correct for fern rhizome scales (attached just inside the base, with overlapping basal lobes, so they look peltate). It sits correctly beside peltate under 'attachment quality'.

label: semi-elliptic
reason: A clear 2-D outline, built like PATO:0002232 semicircular. PATO has no such term.

label: phyllodioicous
definition: A dioicous quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its dwarf male plants growing epiphytically on the leaves or tomentum of the female plants.
reason: Phyllodioicy is a kind of dioicy (separate male and female plants, with dwarf males on the females). It belongs under FLOPO:0991211 dioicous, not directly under 'phenotypic sex'. The current text is also not in the 'X quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of...' form.

label: locellate
reason: Correct: anther locules divided by septa into smaller chambers (locelli). 'structure' is a reasonable parent. The 'fruit' bearer is a data-mapping question.

label: doubly toothed
reason: Correct, as the general class above doubly serrate. PATO:0001205 dentated has 'toothed' as a synonym, so the parent fits. FLOPO:0991221 doubly serrate could be placed under it (its serrated parent sits under dentated in PATO).

label: gonioautoicous
reason: Correct: bud-like male structures in leaf axils just below the female ones, on the same stem. It is a form of autoicy, so the parent is right.

label: monoicous
reason: Correct as the bryophyte counterpart of monoecious. It is the umbrella term for autoicous, synoicous and paroicous, so FLOPO:0991093 autoicous and FLOPO:0991252 synoicous should become its children (a fix to those classes, not this one).

label: bistratose
reason: Correct, and the counterpart of FLOPO:0991320 unistratose (which sits under unstratified). 'stratified' is the right parent.

label: palmatisect
reason: Correct, and built the same way as FLOPO:0991155 pinnatisect under PATO:0104362 dissected.

label: glandular-scaly
reason: Correct: covered with peltate glandular scales; glandular-lepidote is a valid synonym. 'scaly' is the right parent.

label: bipinnatisect
reason: Correct and consistent with pinnatisect, just as bipinnatifid sits under pinnatifid.

label: polygamodioecious
definition: A polygamous quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its belonging to a species whose individuals bear either staminate or pistillate flowers together with some bisexual flowers, so that the species is functionally dioecious.
reason: The meaning and parent are right, but the current text describes a single plant even though the term describes the whole species. The new wording uses the species-level form of FLOPO:0991342 gynodioecious.
